written_results: rho_L(v)=(1/(2*pi^2))*sum_(h=1..L)(1-cos(2*pi*h*v))/h^2; 0<=rho-rho_L<=1/(pi^2*L), and rho_L is exactly zero at integers.
The complete anchored kernel keeps three main terms, the endpoint, and the finite history integral. For ab<=x: 0<=K_x(a,b)-K_(x,L)(a,b)<=1/(pi^2*L*sqrt(ab)).
With U=floor(sqrt(x)), F(x)=sum_(a,b<=U)mu(a)mu(b)K_(x,L(x))(a,b), E=B-F: |E(x)|<=4sqrt(x)/(pi^2*L(x)). No positivity of E is asserted.
For L(x)=ceil(x^(1/4)): int_0^T exp(-2t/3)*|E(exp(t))|^2 dt<=96/pi^4 for every T>=0. This is an approximation-error bound, not a bound on F or W.
General error budget for L(x)>=x^q: 16/[pi^4*(2sigma+2q-1)] when sigma>0, q>=0, 2sigma+2q>1. Failure of this majorant at q<=1/6 for sigma=1/3 is not divergence of actual error.
With D=sqrt(864/5)+4sqrt(6)/pi^2: |sqrt(H_(1/3)(T))-sqrt(int_0^T exp(-2t/3)|F(exp(t))|^2dt)|<=D. The remaining uniform F-energy premise is equivalent to the original one-third target.
The retained three main terms 2sqrt(x)R_U^2-3A_U^2+M_U^2/sqrt(x) and both signed finite-mode terms remain together. No arithmetic exponent gain is supplied.
A dyadic supplier I_j<=C*2^(5j/3)/(j+1)^(1+epsilon) would give retained energy <=C*(1+1/epsilon); the supplier is unpaid.
At x=4 the entrywise-nonnegative error kernel has zero (2,2) entry and positive (1,2) entry; its determinant is negative. No quadratic ordering follows from entrywise order.
